title: Extraction of Cyanobacterial Slime from Community Samples and Subsequent Analysis via GC-MS
author: Kelsey Cremin
materials: Filter the resulting pH 7 solutions through Gelman 0.45 mm filter into new test tubes. Then dry the hydrolysates under flowing nitrogen gas. In this set up, place a single branching capillaries from a line splitter into each test tube where it sits about the liquid level, then connect the line to a nitrogen cannister, which is set to allow a steady flow of nitrogen across the sample. In this set up the samples dry to completeness in 30-60 minutes. Hydrolysis NOTE In our experience it is possible that some known monosaccharides fail to derivatise with the above hydrolysis method. Thus, an alternative hydrolysis method would be to use HCl instead of H 2 SO 4 . Such a method would be similar to the one used by Zhu et al. (2014) for amino sugar hydrolysis, where it was found to have high recovery rates. 6 Alternative hydrolysis methods. Weigh 40 mg samples and standards into glass test tubes, to which add 1 mL of 6 Molarity (M) HCl. Then heat this to 105 °C for 08:00:00 on the heat block, inside the chemical fume hood. Adjust this solution to pH 6.5–7.0 with 1 Molarity (M) sodium hydroxide (NaOH), dry by evaporating it under N 2 as above, re-dissolved in 2 mL methanol (MeOH, 99+%). Samples collected in the supernatant after centrifugation, as above. The methanol step will remove the salt formed from neutralisation. Subsequent derivatisation steps after hydrolysis as the same as described from (step 11 onwards).

steps.title: Prepare BG11+ medium with vitamins
steps.instruction: Prepare BG11+ medium supplemented with the full vitamin mix (1000‑× stock) as listed: Biotin 0.020 g L⁻¹ (stock) → 0.00002 g L⁻¹ medium, Folic Acid 0.020 g L⁻¹ → 0.00002 g L⁻¹, Pyridoxin HCl 0.100 g L⁻¹ → 0.0001 g L⁻¹, Thiamine HCl 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹, Riboflavin 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹, Nicotinic Acid 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹, D‑Ca‑Pantothenate 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹, p‑Aminobenzoic Acid 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹, Vitamin B12 0.001 g L⁻¹ → 0.000001 g L⁻¹, Lipoic Acid 0.050 g L⁻¹ → 0.00005 g L⁻¹. Grow cyanobacterial cultures for at least 35 days in this medium; record culture origin and initiation date. Aim for ~200 mL culture (yields 20–30 mg dried slime) or larger volumes if more slime is needed.

steps.title: Pellet cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the grown cultures at 4000 × g, 4 °C for 20 min to pellet the cells. Keep both the cell pellet (contains adherent slime) and the supernatant (contains EPS) for parallel analysis.

steps.title: Filter and freeze supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant into a clean container, filter sequentially through a Nuclepore 5‑mm pore‑size filter and then a Gelman 0.45‑mm membrane filter. Store the filtrate frozen at –4 °C until lyophilisation. This fraction is called “Culture Supernatant”.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet for slime extraction
steps.instruction: Measure the pellet volume, then add ddH₂O equal to 30 × the pellet volume (e.g., 1 mL pellet → 30 mL ddH₂O). Vortex vigorously and store the suspension overnight at 4 °C to allow slime to diffuse into the water.

steps.title: Collect slime from pellet suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overnight suspension at 4000 × g, 4 °C for 20 min. Remove the supernatant (contains slime) and keep it at 4 °C. Retain the cell pellet for further extraction.

steps.title: Iterative pellet washing (five cycles)
steps.instruction: Perform five successive wash cycles on the retained pellet to liberate additional slime.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet (≈5 mL for a 200 mL culture) in 25 mL ddH₂O (scale proportionally with culture size).
Vortex for ≤2 min, then aliquot the suspension into twelve 2‑mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 15000 × g (temperature not specified) for 15 min in a benchtop centrifuge.
Collect the supernatant from each tube, pool all supernatants together.
Resuspend each pellet in 1.5 mL fresh ddH₂O.
Repeat the vortex‑split‑centrifuge‑collect‑resuspend sequence for a total of five cycles (labelled 1/5 through 5/5). By the third cycle the pooled supernatant may acquire a slight blue colour.

steps.title: Final shear of remaining pellet
steps.instruction: Collect the remaining pellets after the fifth wash into one Falcon tube, add 10 mL ddH₂O, and shear by pipetting up and down 20 times through a 10‑mL syringe fitted with an 18 G needle, then repeat 20 times with a 25 G needle. Centrifuge again (conditions as above), collect the supernatant and add it to the pooled supernatants from the previous washes. Keep the final pellet (named “Culture cyano pellet”) for later analysis.

steps.title: Calcium precipitation of slime
steps.instruction: To the combined supernatant (final volume ≈90 mL) add 45 mg CaCl₂ to obtain a final CaCl₂ concentration of 500 mg L⁻¹. Mix thoroughly and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Pellet precipitated slime
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the CaCl₂‑treated solution at 15000 × g (temperature not specified) for 30 min. Discard the clear supernatant and retain the green‑tinged gelatinous pellet (named “Culture slime pellet”, final volume <1 mL) and the supernatant (named “Culture slime supernatant”) in the fridge for later use.

steps.title: Lyophilise all fractions
steps.instruction: Lyophilise the following fractions separately: Culture Supernatant, Culture cyano pellet, Culture slime supernatant, and Culture slime pellet.

steps.title: Prepare monosaccharide standards and blanks
steps.instruction: Prepare HPLC‑grade monosaccharide standards (Glucose, Xylose, Galactose, Mannose, Rhamnose, Galacturonic acid, Galactonate, Gluconarate, D‑Fructose, L‑Fucose, Adonitol, Fumaric acid, L‑Aspartic acid, L‑Arabinose) at 1 mg L⁻¹ by serial dilution. Include two blanks: fresh BG11+ medium with vitamin mix and ddH₂O.

steps.title: First stage acid hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Weigh 40 mg of each lyophilised sample, each standard, and each blank into separate clean glass vials. Add 1.5 mL of 72 % aqueous H₂SO₄ to each vial. Stir at room temperature for 2 h (02:00:00).

steps.title: Second stage hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL H₂O to each vial, then heat in an oven at 80 °C for 1 h (01:00:00). Cool the tubes in an ice bath and store at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Neutralise hydrolysates
steps.instruction: Adjust each hydrolysate to pH 7 by adding solid Na₂CO₃ until CO₂ evolution ceases (large amount of Na₂CO₃ may be required, forming carbonate salts).

steps.title: Trimethylsilylation – pyridine dissolution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried hydrolysates in 1.5 mL pyridine (≥99 %). Shake by hand for 30 s, then incubate at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Add TMS‑imidazole and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL 1‑(Trimethylsilyl)imidazole (≥97 %) to each tube and incubate in a shaking incubator at 60 °C (duration as required for complete silylation).

steps.title: Remove pyridine under nitrogen
steps.instruction: Cool the tubes to room temperature, then evaporate pyridine completely with a gentle stream of nitrogen gas (30–60 min). Perform this step in a fume hood due to pyridine odor.

steps.title: Heptane washes to eliminate pyridine
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL heptane (≥99.3 % LC grade) to each dried sample, evaporate under nitrogen, and repeat the addition and drying cycle several times until no pyridine odor remains.

steps.title: Prepare GC master stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve each 40 mg TMS‑derivatised sample in 8 mL hexane (≥99 % LC grade) to obtain a 5 mg mL⁻¹ master stock.

steps.title: Dilute to working concentration
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the master stock into a brown glass GC vial and dilute with hexane to a final volume of 1 mL, yielding a 5 mg L⁻¹ working solution. Avoid any precipitate; only the clear solution should be used for injection.

steps.title: Store TMS derivatives if needed
steps.instruction: If analysis cannot be performed immediately, seal the vials moisture‑tight and store at –20 °C; the TMS derivatives remain stable for several months.

steps.title: GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Run all samples on an Agilent 7890GC coupled to a 5977B MSD detector using an HP‑5MS column (30 m × 250 mm × 0.25 mm, 5 % phenyl‑methyl‑silox). Set initial oven temperature to 150 °C, hold 2 min, ramp 8 °C min⁻¹ to 250 °C, hold 17 min. Helium carrier gas flow 1.2 mL min⁻¹. Front inlet 275 °C, transfer line 280 °C, MS source 230 °C, quadrupole 150 °C. Inject 1 mL (as written) at 6000 µL min⁻¹. Total run time 32 min. Use electron ionisation, scan 50–750 m/z.
